title: Extension by zero under a proper modification
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $\pi:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $U'=Y\times_XU$ [def-pc-fibre-product], let $j':U'\hookrightarrow Y$ be its open immersion and $h:U'\to U$ its projection, and assume $h$ is an isomorphism. For any sheaf $G$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], put $G'=h^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. With extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the canonical adjunction map is an isomorphism and the positive higher direct images vanish:
$$
 j_!G\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_*j'_!G',\qquad R^q\pi_*j'_!G'=0\quad(q>0).
$$
Here the canonical map is adjoint under $\pi^{-1}\dashv\pi_*$ to the inverse of the extension-by-zero base-change map $j'_!h^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi^{-1}j_!G$. No finiteness or constructibility of $G$ and no invertibility assumption on $\#\Lambda$ is required.

proof.text: Put F = j'_! h^{-1}G and E = j_!G. Apply the existing source-library derived comparison [lem-finrepair-existing-derived-modification-comparison] to the chosen pullback square. It gives an isomorphism Rπ_*(F[0]) ≅ E[0], without specifying the comparison arrow. The degree-zero homology isomorphisms for total right derived functors and the left-exact functor π_* give π_*F ≅ E. These are Functor.homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso and Functor.rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf in the Lean proof.

Let J=j_!, L=π^{-1}, R=π_*. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], the transformation b: h^{-1} ⋙ j'_! → J ⋙ L is invertible. The functor h^{-1} is an equivalence because h is an isomorphism (the isomorphism case of [prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos]); j'_! is fully faithful by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso]. Thus J ⋙ L is fully faithful. The unit of its composite adjunction is invertible. Its component is η_J(G) followed by j^{-1}(η_L(E)); since η_J is invertible, j^{-1}(η_L(E)) is invertible.

The exact stated map a is η_L(E) followed by R(b^{-1}_G), by the homEquiv formula for the adjunction. Therefore j^{-1}(a) is invertible by the previous step. Both E and R(F) are in the essential image of J: E=J(G), and R(F)≅E by step 1. The counit of J ⊣ j^{-1} is invertible on this essential image since J is fully faithful. Its naturality identity J(j^{-1}(a)) ε_{R(F)} = ε_E a expresses a as a composite of isomorphisms. This proves invertibility of the specified arrow, without identifying it with the noncanonical object isomorphism of step 1. The Lean facts used here are Adjunction.isIso_counit_app_of_iso and counit.naturality.

Use the compatibility of bounded-below and unbounded total right derived functors (Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility) to identify the object defining higherDirectImage with the unbounded object in step 1. Apply H^q to its isomorphism with E[0]. For q>0 the homology of E[0] is zero, since a single object in degree zero is cohomologically at most zero. Transport zero along this homology isomorphism.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N5-d59bbcbd3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 14 cited nodes in full, and checked the Stacks sources at the cited places: 03S6 l.11493, 03S5 l.11425, 03Q1 l.4649, 0DDF l.18734, 04JN l.8732, plus 03PU, 0D6J, 07A7 and 02GP in tags/tags. The delivery itself changes only two things against the side-DAG copy: the item's status goes from unsplit to split, and its Mathlib searches are refreshed. It creates no new nodes. The statement matches the master and main-20261015 blueprint, hypothesis by hypothesis. It assumes a finite commutative Λ, a proper π, an open immersion j with h: U'→U an isomorphism, and an arbitrary Λ-module sheaf G. The canonical map is the adjoint of the inverse of the j_! base-change map, exactly as in the Lean binding (homEquiv applied to inv of etaleLowerShriekBaseChangeMap, ModuleCat Λ, [Finite Λ]). Nothing is weakened. Small cases checked: U empty, U=X, Y empty, Λ=0, and points inside and outside U. Step 1: 03S6 applies to the cartesian square because the open extension by zero is the étale-sum extension with at most one lift, by the definition's own statement. Step 2: the cited corollary needs only Λ finite and K bounded below, which F[0] satisfies. Step 3: outside U the stalks are zero, and conservativity applies. Step 4 is the long step (2608 characters). It is one argument: the fibre is Spec Ω, the stalks are identified, and a germ computation gives c·b·t·a = id. The degree-zero identification of the derived exchange with the underived exchange is three lines from lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients (3) and lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise. The existing candidates lem-sbc-base-change-homology-zero-underived (states it only up to isomorphism of arrows and does not pass through the forgetful comparison of coefficients) and lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology (abelian only) are off-route and fit no better, so the step may stay. Step 5: exactness of inverse image and stalks as global sections over Spec Ω give the vanishing and the isomorphism. I found no duplicate of the item in the DAG, no cycle and no SGA citation. I accept the 9 declared tool_uses of generic proper-base-change and stalk nodes. No fixes.
